title: The AML-Associated A338V Mutation Rewires GPR183 Signaling through C-Terminal Ensemble Redistribution.
authors: Andersson, Louise; Wesolowski, Patryk A; Jahrstorfer, Laura; Rosa, Alexander De; Heger, Tomas; Neuman, Vilmos; Sieradzan, Adam K; Wales, David J; Kozielewicz, Pawel
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
one_liner_zh: 该研究结合分子动力学模拟与实验，解析AML相关GPR183 A338V突变通过重塑C端无序区构象ensemble选择性调控G蛋白与arrestin信号，属于蛋白质构象计算与功能关联研究，对GPCR构象采样方法有参考价值。
abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) rely on dynamic conformational ensembles to coordinate G protein activation and recruitment of regulatory transducers such as GPCR kinases and beta-arrestins. The oxysterol receptor GPR183 has been implicated in hematological malignancies, including acute myeloid leukemia (AML), where a rare A338V substitution occurs within its intrinsically disordered C-terminal tail. Here, we combined bioluminescence/fluorescence resonance energy transfer, bioluminescence- and fluorescence-based assays as well as migration experiments, with molecular dynamics simulations and allosteric communication networks to define the structural and functional consequences of this mutation. The A338V variant preserved agonist potency and largely maintained or even enhanced agonist-induced Gi protein activation, likely by inducing different receptor core conformations. On the other hand, it consistently impaired GRK2 and beta-arrestin2 recruitment across multiple experimental configurations. Atomistic simulations supported these observations and further suggested that A338V reshapes the conformational ensemble of the C-terminal tail, altering its disorder, compaction, and membrane interactions. In particular, the mutation redistributes lipid interactions of phosphorylation-prone serine and threonine residues within the tail, suggesting disrupted spatial presentation of regulatory motifs required for productive GRK2 and beta-arrestin coupling. Importantly, overexpression of GPR183 A338V in differentiated HL-60 cells led to a significant increase in migration of these cells toward the chemoattractant. Together, these results identify the intrinsically disordered C-terminal tail of GPR183 as a determinant of selective transducer coupling and show how a single naturally occurring mutation within a GPCR intrinsically disordered region can alter its conformational ensemble, selectively modulate intracellular protein coupling, and affect receptor-mediated cellular behavior.
abstract_zh: G蛋白偶联受体（GPCRs）依赖动态构象集合来协调G蛋白激活及调控性转导因子（如GPCR激酶和β-arrestins）的招募。氧固醇受体GPR183已被涉及血液恶性肿瘤，包括急性髓系白血病（AML），其中在其 intrinsically disordered C末端尾部发生罕见的A338V替换。在此，我们结合生物发光/荧光共振能量转移、基于生物发光和荧光的检测以及迁移实验，与分子动力学模拟和变构通信网络相结合，以确定该突变的结构和功能后果。A338V变体保留了激动剂效力，并在很大程度上维持甚至增强了激动剂诱导的Gi蛋白激活，可能通过诱导不同的受体核心构象实现。另一方面，在多种实验配置中，它一致地损害了GRK2和β-arrestin2的招募。原子级模拟支持这些观察结果，并进一步表明A338V重塑了C末端尾部的构象集合，改变其无序性、压缩性和膜相互作用。特别是，该突变重新分配了尾部内易磷酸化的丝氨酸和苏氨酸残基的脂质相互作用，提示破坏了对有效GRK2和β-arrestin偶联所需的调控基序的空间呈现。重要的是，在分化的HL-60细胞中过表达GPR183 A338V导致这些细胞向趋化因子的迁移显著增加。总之，这些结果将GPR183的 intrinsically disordered C末端尾部确定为选择性转导因子偶联的决定因素，并展示了GPCR intrinsically disordered区域内单个自然发生的突变如何改变其构象集合、选择性调节细胞内蛋白偶联，并影响受体介导的细胞行为。
